method: Synthetic open cases (the time_sweep.py `daily` mixture: eleven open states, ~40% overdue, previous sweep one working day before the timed one, cases.next_due_at as the last append left it) are seeded by several processes with COPY into a template database on the in-cluster Postgres (kind cluster sc-m76, postgres-0, tools/k8s/postgres.yaml), then VACUUM (ANALYZE)d. Each timed cell recreates `closure_load` from the template (file copy), runs a CHECKPOINT, then times ONE sweep at the fixed sweep time (2026-03-10 08:00 UTC): workers=1 is app.sweep.run_sweep in one process with a TimedStore that accumulates the time spent inside the store's read and append calls (planning is wall - read - append); workers=N is POST /scheduler/sweep on the FastAPI app (in process, TestClient) with SWEEP_WORKERS=N and a warm worker pool, as the scheduler service triggers it. A second identical sweep (idle re-sweep, must emit nothing) is timed, then an untimed full-scan sweep (every case read and replayed; timed separately as the no-index cost) must find nothing left to do. Correctness assertions are those of time_sweep.py (emitted == planner expectation, no errors/rejects, no close event, gap-free logs, row count grew by exactly the events emitted). The sweep runs on the macOS host (the Python process) and reaches Postgres through the kind port mapping and the Docker VM, so every statement pays that hop; the API pods in the cluster reach Postgres over the pod network. The host, the Docker VM (10 CPUs, ~7.7 GiB) and the three kind nodes are shared by the load generator, Postgres and the cluster's own pods.
